run: OmniVoice adapted to Persian by its official recipe, on Kaggle T4 pairs
status: session a v1 cancelled after stalling in its download stage; nothing trained - see outcomes

recipe.source: k2-fsa/OmniVoice 08be0b4ccbac3e13e374e86fbfead4b4cac343e2, examples/config/train_config_finetune_sdpa.json (git blob 4b0a543e23be), fetched and checked in every session
recipe.values: lr 1e-5, AdamW weight decay 0.01, cosine schedule with 1% warmup, 5,000 steps, 8,192 tokens per GPU on two GPUs, no gradient accumulation, gradient norm clip 1.0, bf16 mixed precision, language_ratio 0.8, prompt ratio 0-0.3, mask ratio 0-1, condition drop 0.1, codebook weights [8,8,6,6,4,4,2,2], seed 42, evaluation and checkpoint every 500 steps
recipe.data: eval/manifests/adaptation_splits_v1.jsonl.gz: train 87,499 clips, 127.85 h, 3,835 speakers (Common Voice 26 cleaned + Neyshekar v6); valid 2,251 clips, 3.68 h; language_id fa
changes_on_this_hardware: gradient checkpointing on the LLM and DDP gradient_as_bucket_view - memory only; probe v2 showed the same first loss and first-step gradients as the official path
base and tokenizer loaded from local snapshots of their pinned revisions
keep_last_n_checkpoints 1 and a float16 export every 1,000 steps - retention, not training
sessions stop after an official checkpoint and resume through the official resume_from_checkpoint, which restarts the data order at the first epoch

a.does: writes and tokenises train and valid (never a test clip; Neyshekar's test shards are not even downloaded), then trains from the base until a checkpoint is the last that fits 11.25 hours from the notebook's start
a.expected: about 4 h of data and tokenising, then about 1,500 steps; about 10.5 GPU-hours

c.does: resumes from b's checkpoint and finishes at 5,000

sessions.then: one development-set session scoring the five float16 exports and the published model in the same kernel, about 1 GPU-hour

budget_declared_before_the_push.total: about 25-26 GPU-hours of T4 x2: 19.4 h of training at probe v2's 13.98 s a step, 3.6 h of tokenising at 36x real time, evaluations, start-ups, saves, and the time lost stopping at a checkpoint rather than at the session's end
budget_declared_before_the_push.quota: about 30 GPU-hours a week. The API does not report what is left or when the week turns over; this week's earlier kernels (the MOSS v1.5 runs of 2026-09-18, Fish and Higgs of 2026-09-17, the two probes) used some of it. If a session cannot start or is cut short for quota, the last checkpoint stands and the next session resumes from it after the reset
budget_declared_before_the_push.stops: each session stops by itself 11.25 h after its notebook starts, with at least 10 minutes' margin before its 12-hour limit; no session starts training with less than 2.3 hours left

reading_fixed_before_the_run: SOTA_ROADMAP.md section 8: the exports at 1,000-5,000 steps are scored on the development set beside the published model in one session; the one with the highest held-out similarity whose CER interval against the published model does not lie above zero is the candidate; only that candidate and the published model are then scored, once, on the sealed test sets (primary: the 28 usable Neyshekar test speakers; secondary: the 30 Common Voice ones), H0 delta <= 0, one-sided alpha 0.025. The training losses are not a quality result, and no improvement is claimed before the test comparison

session_a_v1.ended: status KernelWorkerStatus.CANCEL_ACKNOWLEDGED, first read by the watcher at 18:10 UTC; it read RUNNING at every earlier check, the last by hand at 08:55 UTC. Nobody here cancelled it; whether Kaggle's session limit or a manual cancel ended it is not recorded anywhere this project can read
session_a_v1.what_the_log_shows: the pinned stack installed and verified, two T4s, the runner gate passed at 137 s; at 138 s the download cell began (two Hugging Face 'unauthenticated requests' warnings) and no line was written after that
session_a_v1.not_produced: no data, tokens, checkpoint, export or gate record past the runner
session_a_v1.cause: [hypothesis, strongly suggested] a network call in the download cell blocked without a time limit: that cell ran snapshot_download four times (about 21 GiB: base 3.04, tokenizer 0.75, Common Voice 6.94, Neyshekar train and valid 10.22) and urllib.request.urlopen with no timeout, inside the notebook's own process, where nothing bounded it. At normal Kaggle speeds 21 GiB takes minutes, so this was a stall, not slowness; which call stalled is not in the log
session_a_v1.gpu_time_spent: the T4 pair was held from 01:14 UTC until the session ended - at least the 7 h 41 min to the last RUNNING read, probably Kaggle's 12-hour limit - for nothing
